title: Provider manifest
description:
A declarative description of one upstream data source. Providers are declared, never hard-coded: adding a feed is writing one of these, and a provider that cannot be described here is a provider Archie will not fetch.

The manifest carries no credentials. It names the secret it needs; the secret itself lives in the node's secret store and never reaches the manifest, the renderer, or a log line.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. `usgs.earthquakes`. Referenced by every record this provider produces.

capability.description: The Archie capability this provider satisfies, e.g. `world.seismic`. A node without that capability will not load the provider, which is how an operator turns whole domains on and off.

access.description: How the provider is reached and under what terms.

authentication.description: `none` is the preferred case and covers most authoritative government feeds.

secret_handle.description: NAME of the secret required, never the secret. Resolved at fetch time from the node's secret store. Required whenever `authentication` is not `none`; a manifest that needs a credential and does not name one cannot be satisfied.

attribution.description: Rendered wherever this provider's records are displayed, when the access class requires it.

cadence.description: How often to poll, and what the provider permits. Archie treats a quota as a hard limit, not a target: exceeding one is how an operator loses access to a feed they depend on.

min_poll_seconds.description: Floor imposed by the provider's terms. The scheduler may never poll faster, whatever the configuration says.

backoff.description: What to do when the provider errors or rate-limits. Every provider gets a backoff policy: a feed that fails must not become a feed that hammers.

coverage.description: What this provider can and cannot see. Stating the limits is what stops an absence of data being read as an absence of events.

geographic.description: A regional provider reporting nothing outside its region is not evidence that nothing happened there.

known_gaps.description: Documented blind spots, e.g. 'ADS-B coverage is sparse over open ocean' or 'military aircraft frequently disable transponders'. Rendered alongside the layer.

latency_seconds.description: Typical delay between the phenomenon and the provider publishing it.

records.description: Which normalized record types this provider yields. A provider that cannot be mapped onto the normalized model does not get an ad-hoc passthrough; the model is extended instead, so the renderer never receives arbitrary provider JSON.

state.description: Runtime state, reported to the display so a dark layer is explained rather than merely dark. `no_credentials` is the ordinary state of an optional provider on a node whose operator has not configured it, and is not an error.

allOf.$comment: A provider that authenticates must name the secret it needs. Without this rule a manifest can silently depend on an ambient credential, which is how a key ends up in an environment variable nobody documented.
